work_item.title: Dark/Light Theme Implementation
work_item.description: 🚩 AC Addressed (Required) Introduce light/dark theme selection entirely within the existing Python-rendered web UI. Ensure query syntax highlighting and result panels remain legible under both themes. Persist the user’s theme choice across requests using local storage. 💡 What do you want to accomplish? (Required) Improve user experience by allow users to toggle between dark/light themes. 📋 Testability Considerations (Required) Unit tests to check the new dark/light theme functionality.
acceptance_criteria: Users can toggle between dark and light themes via the UI
Syntax highlighting colors adjust appropriately for both themes and remain readable
Result panels adapt styling to maintain legibility under both themes
User's theme preference is saved in local storage and applied on subsequent page loads
Unit tests cover theme toggle functionality and persistence

analysis.summary: Implement a toggle for dark and light themes in the existing Python-rendered web UI, ensuring syntax highlighting and result panels remain legible, with user preference persisted via local storage.
technical_requirements: Add light/dark theme toggle functionality within the existing Python-rendered web UI
Ensure query syntax highlighting is legible in both themes
Ensure result panels are legible in both themes
Persist user theme choice across requests using local storage
Implement unit tests to verify dark/light theme functionality

risks: Ensuring consistent styling and legibility across all UI components under both themes
Maintaining compatibility with existing Python-rendered UI without introducing regressions

analysis.recommended_approach: Introduce CSS classes for dark and light themes and toggle them via JavaScript integrated into the Python-rendered UI. Update syntax highlighting styles to support both themes. Use local storage to save and retrieve the user's theme preference on page load. Add unit tests to verify theme toggling and persistence behavior.

implementation_steps.description: Add theme CSS styles with CSS variables for light and dark themes in styles.py and update existing styles to use these variables

instructions: Define CSS variables for light theme colors: --bg-color: #f8f9fa, --text-color: #333333, --primary-color: #0066cc, --syntax-keyword: #00008b, --syntax-string: #a31515, --syntax-comment: #008000, --result-bg: #ffffff, --result-text: #000000.

Define CSS variables for dark theme colors under a .dark-theme class: --bg-color: #1a1a1a, --text-color: #e0e0e0, --primary-color: #4da6ff, --syntax-keyword: #569cd6, --syntax-string: #d69d85, --syntax-comment: #6a9955, --result-bg: #2d2d2d, --result-text: #f0f0f0.
Refactor existing body and container styles to use the CSS variables for background and text colors, e.g., body { background-color: var(--bg-color); color: var(--text-color); }.
Update syntax highlighting styles to use the new CSS variables for keywords, strings, and comments to ensure readability in both themes.
Update result panel styles to use --result-bg and --result-text variables for background and text colors respectively.
Add CSS for the theme toggle button styling using variables for colors to ensure consistency.

implementation_steps.validation: CSS in styles.py includes both light and dark theme variables, existing styles use these variables, and syntax highlighting and result panel styles adapt accordingly.

implementation_steps.description: Add theme toggle button to the base HTML template and integrate JavaScript for theme toggling and persistence using localStorage

instructions: Locate the main HTML template rendering function or variable that defines the base layout.
Insert a theme toggle button in the header or navigation bar area with id='theme-toggle' and class='theme-toggle-btn', with initial text '🌙 Dark Mode'.
Add a <script> block before the closing </body> tag containing JavaScript that:
- On page load, reads the 'theme' value from localStorage.
- Applies the 'dark-theme' CSS class to the <body> element if the stored theme is 'dark'.
- Updates the toggle button text to '☀️ Light Mode' if dark theme is active, otherwise '🌙 Dark Mode'.
- Adds a click event listener to the toggle button that toggles the 'dark-theme' class on <body>, updates localStorage with the new theme, and updates the button text accordingly.
Ensure the JavaScript is vanilla JS and compatible with existing page scripts.

implementation_steps.validation: The base HTML template includes a theme toggle button and JavaScript that correctly applies and persists the theme preference using localStorage.

implementation_steps.description: Add unit tests for theme toggle functionality and persistence in presentation/tests/test_theme_toggle.py

instructions: Create tests that simulate rendering the base HTML template and verify the presence of the theme toggle button.
Test that the JavaScript for theme toggling is included in the rendered HTML.
Use a headless browser testing framework or mock DOM environment to simulate clicking the toggle button and verify that the 'dark-theme' class is toggled on the body element.
Test that the theme preference is saved to and read from localStorage correctly.
Include tests for default theme application when no preference is set.
Ensure tests are runnable with existing test infrastructure.

implementation_steps.validation: Unit tests cover UI presence, JavaScript functionality, and localStorage persistence of theme preference.

implementation.pr_description: Implemented dark/light theme toggle feature with CSS variables in styles.py, added toggle button and JavaScript in html_template.py for user interaction and localStorage persistence, and created unit tests to verify theme toggle functionality and persistence.
